newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch share yields surged in 1996 -- stats bureau.
newsitem.headline: Dutch share yields surged in 1996 -- stats bureau.

text.p: Yields on investments in shares listed on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange were 37 percent in 1996, more than double the 17 percent average over the last 13 years, the Dutch Central Bureau of Statistics (CBS) said on Monday.
"In those 13 years the yield on share investments was only higher (than 37 percent) in 1993," the CBS said in a statement.

The yield scored on the Dutch bourse was also considerably higher than world averages, with the Morgan Stanley Capital Index (MSCI) rising by 23 percent this year. It is the fifth consecutive year that Amsterdam outperformed world averages.
Dutch small and mid-sized bourse-listed companies performed considerably better than the larger firms.

The Dutch price index for smaller and medium-sized companies showed, one week before the end of 1996, a year-on-year rise of 52 percent whereas the Amsterdam AEX index, which groups the 25 most actively traded firms, rose by 30 percent.
Last year the pattern was the other way around with large bourse-listed companies outperforming the smaller ones.
The yield on investments in the Dutch bond market was eight percent in the year so far, slightly below the nine percent average posted in the last 13 years.
Of the bourse-listed investment funds, the ones that limit themselves to Dutch shares performed best this year with a yield of 36 percent.
Funds investing worldwide in shares scored lower with a yield of 25 percent but still outperformed world averages which totalled 23 percent, the CBS said.
